title: Overloads that switch themselves off
description:
Write two overloads of `twice`:

- for integral types it returns `value * 2`;
- for floating-point types it returns `value * 2.0` **rounded to the nearest whole number** (`std::round`), as the same floating type.

Any other type must have **no** matching overload at all (not a compile error deep inside the function: the call itself must be rejected).

Do it the pre-C++20 way with `std::enable_if_t` in the template parameter list, to see how it reads:

```cpp
template <typename T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_integral_v<T>, int> = 0>
```

(When you are done, try rewriting it with `std::integral` and `std::floating_point`. The tests accept either.)
hints: Add a second, unnamed template parameter: `template <typename T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_integral_v<T>, int> = 0>`. For other types it has no `type`, so the overload is removed.
The floating-point overload uses `std::is_floating_point_v<T>` and returns `std::round(value * 2.0)` converted back to `T`.
